```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
# Add any other libraries here



```


```{r load-data}
rawdata <- read_csv("data/ames.csv")


```

```{r data}

# Preparing data
data <- rawdata %>%
  select(price, area, Year.Built, Yr.Sold, Year.Remod.Add, Bedroom.AbvGr, Overall.Qual, Overall.Cond, Garage.Cars, Fireplaces, Kitchen.AbvGr, Full.Bath, Half.Bath) %>%
  rename(bedrooms = Bedroom.AbvGr) %>%
  rename(kitchens = Kitchen.AbvGr) %>%
  mutate(
    Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold = Yr.Sold - Year.Remod.Add,
    Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built = Year.Remod.Add - Year.Built,
    If.Remodelled = case_when(
      Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built == 0 ~ "No",
      Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built > 0 ~ "Yes"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    bathrooms = Full.Bath + (0.5 * Half.Bath)
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

options(scipen = 999)

# medans and medians
median_price <- median(data$price)
mean_price <- mean(data$price)
sd_price <- sd(data$price)
median_bedrooms <- median(data$bedrooms)
mean_bedrooms <- mean(data$bedrooms)
median_area <- median(data$area)
mean_area <- mean(data$area)
sd_area <- sd(data$area)



#graphs

# house prices density plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "lightblue",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Density Distribution of House Prices",
    x = "House Price ($)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
      geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_price,
    colour = "red", # median is red!!
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_price,
    colour = "orange", # mean is orange 
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, max(data$price), by = 100000),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# analysis - graph is positively skewed. Mean > Median > Mode
# this means that most house prices are below the mean
# this means that most people earn moderate amounts but a few earn very high incomes

# histogram for bedrooms per house in ames, iowa
ggplot(data, aes(x = bedrooms)) +
  geom_histogram(
    fill = "darkcyan",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_bedrooms,
    colour = "orange", # orange is the mean of data, else is median
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Bedrooms in Houses in Ames, Iowa",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms per House",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# area of different houses
ggplot(data, aes(x = area)) +
  geom_histogram(
    fill = "darkturquoise",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
    geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_area,
    colour = "red", # median is red!!
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_area,
    colour = "orange", # orange is the mean of data, else is median
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Area of Houses in Ames, Iowa",
    x = "Area",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Scatterplot graphs for relationships

# Graph 1: Price vs Area
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = area, y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Area",
    x = "Area",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)


# Graph 2: Price vs Year Built
p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Year.Built, y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Year Built",
    x = "Year Built",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p2)


# Graph 3: Price vs Year Sold
p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(Yr.Sold), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "purple",
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "House Price Distribution by Year Sold",
    x = "Year Sold",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p3)


# Graph 4: Price vs Year Remodelled
p4 <- ggplot(data %>% 
               filter(If.Remodelled == "Yes"),
  aes(x = Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built, 
      y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "orange", 
             size = 2, 
             alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Years Between Building and Remodelling",
    x = "Years Between Building and Remodelling",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p4)

# Graph 5: Price vs No. of  Bedrooms
p5 <- ggplot(data, 
             aes(x = factor(bedrooms), 
                 y = price)
             ) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "yellow", 
               color = "red", 
               alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Number of Bedrooms",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p5)

# area vs number of bedrooms
p6 <- ggplot(data, 
             aes(x = factor(bedrooms), 
                 y = area)
             ) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "pink", 
               color = "red", 
               alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "House Area vs Number of Bedrooms",
    x = "Number of Bedrooms",
    y = "Area"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p6)

# Graph 7: Price vs Years Between Remodelling and Year Sold
p7 <- ggplot(data %>% 
               filter(If.Remodelled == "Yes"),
             aes(x = Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold, 
                 y = price)) +
  geom_point(color = "plum", 
             size = 2, 
             alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "House Price vs Years Between Remodelling and Sale",
    x = "Years Between Remodelling and Sale",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p7)

# Graph 8: Comparing if houses have or haven't been remodelled

p8 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = If.Remodelled, 
                 y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkmagenta") +
  labs(
    title = "House Prices: Remodelled vs Not Remodelled",
    x = "Has the House Been Remodelled?",
    y = "House Price"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p8)

```
``` {r stats}
# Correlations calculations
correlations <- data %>%
  summarise(
    Price_Area_Cor = cor(price, area),
    Price_Yr_Built_Cor = cor(price, Year.Built),
    Price_Yr_Sold_Cor = cor(price, Yr.Sold),
    Price_Yr_Remodelled_Cor = cor(price, Year.Remod.Add),
    Price_Bedrooms = cor(price, bedrooms),
    Price_Btwn_Remod_Built_Cor = cor(price, Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Built),
    Price_Btwn_Remod_Sale_Cor = cor(price, Remod.Year.Vs.Year.Sold)
  )

print(correlations)

#other stats
stats <- data %>%
  summarise(
    mean_price,
    median_price,
    sd_price,
    mean_bedrooms,
    median_bedrooms,
    mean_area,
    median_area,
    sd_area
  )

# y-intercept and gradients *key for report*
# The regression analysis shows a ___itive relationship between...

# Price vs Area
summary(lm(price ~ area, data = data))
# gradient = ~111.7, y-intercept = ~13,290, R^2 = ~0.4995

# Price vs Year Built
summary(lm(price ~ Year.Built, data = data))
# gradient = ~1475, y-intercept = ~-2,727,000, R^2 = ~0.3118

# Price vs Year Remodelled
summary(lm(price ~ Year.Remod.Add, data = data))
# gradient = ~2,041, y-intercept = ~3,869,000, R^2 = ~0.2841

# All data altogether
summary(lm(price ~ area + bedrooms + Overall.Qual + Overall.Cond + kitchens + bathrooms, 
           data = data))
# analysis: 
# using a 5% significance level we can see overall condition and number of bathrooms is insignificant
# each extra unit of area adds ~$74.23
# each extra bedroom lowers price by about $11,858 (maybe bc model already accounts for overall area? For houses of same area, having more bedrooms could indicate smaller individual rooms.)
# each 1 point increase in quality adds $29,397 (strongest effect as t = ~39.94). t is estimate / std error aka how many standard errors the coefficient is away from 0
# overall condition has a -57.95 coefficient. But p value is 0.933 which is considearbly higher than 0.05 there is insufficient statistical evidence to suggest that overall condition has an independent relationship with house prices after controlling for the other variables.
# kitchen coefficient is -$24,227. hmm weird
# bathrooms is +$2,084 where +1 bathroom is full bathroom and +0.5 bathroom is a half bathroom. (so like toilet only). 
# intercept isnt meaningful as it is -$53,876. a house will never have no area and no bedrooms and no... etc.
# R^2 = 0.7469: six independent variables together explain about 74.69% of variation in price. remaining 25.31% is unexplained by model and may be influenced by other factors like location.
# Residual standard error = 40,240 so predictions are typically off by about $40,240

# Price = -53,876.395 + 74.229(Area) - 11,857.795(Bedrooms) + 29,396.574(Overall Quality) - 57.951(Overall Condition) - 24,226.913(Kitchens) + 2,084.198(Bathrooms)

# all data together only with variables that are significant:
summary(lm(price ~ area + bedrooms + Overall.Qual + kitchens,
           data = data))
# new regression equation
# Price = -55,321.418 + 75.493(Area) - 11,667.601(Bedrooms) + 29,676.702(Overall Quality) - 23,616.444(Kitchens)
# R^2 = 0.7468: The model explains 74.68% of the variation in house prices.
# RSE (residual standard error) = 40,240
# Yay!
```
